small.def.v: Small-cluster readings (post hoc, robustness). est = headline estimate (item-pooled mean; for ratios, AUROC differences and P5' the statistic itself). t_ci = estimate +- t(G-1, 0.975) x SE with the cluster-robust SE  sqrt(G/(G-1) sum_g (sum_{i in g}(d_i - mean))^2)/n  (G = 11 or 19 databases); tdb_ci = t(G-1) interval of the unweighted mean of the database-level mean differences; sf_ci / sfu_ci = {theta0 : exact two-sided sign-flip p > 0.05} over the G database-level mean differences with weights n_g/n (sf) or 1/G (sfu), all 2^G sign patterns enumerated; for statistics that are not item means (ratios of sums, AUROC and AURC differences, P5') t and sign-flip use delete-one-database jackknife pseudo-values (tdb = t, sfu = sf). cl_ci and item_ci are the intervals of RV2.dual (database-clustered percentile and item bootstrap, B = 10 000); wide_ci = hull(cl, item, t, sf), wideu_ci = hull of all six, old_ci = hull(cl, item). class_* = reading word under the rule of the contrast (RV2.dual.<id>.rule) applied to that interval; reading_changes = yes when the word of wide_ci differs from that of old_ci (reading_changes_u: wideu_ci). p_* = two-sided p for H0: theta = null (0, the margin -1.5 for NI(1.5), 0.80 or 1 for the ratio rules). Smallest attainable two-sided sign-flip p: 2^(1-G) = 0.00098 (G = 11), 0.0000038 (G = 19).

small.pstar.def.v: Family P* (Holm over P1', W1, P3, P5', m = 4, one-sided p doubled, SAP 15.3) re-tested with the database as the unit: p_sf1 = exact one-sided sign-flip p over the 11 database-level values (weights n_g/n, the headline estimand; p_sfu1 with equal weights), p_t1 = one-sided cluster-robust t(10) p; P1' EX end point against -1.5 pp, P1' calls ratio against 0.80, W1 and P3 against 0; the ratio and the AUROC difference use delete-one-database jackknife pseudo-values. P1' needs both end points (maximum). P5' keeps its exact McNemar p (not a cluster test). holds_sf and holds_t = Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 AND the hull of cl, item, t, sf satisfies the rule; holds_sfu = the same with the equal-weight sign-flip p and the hull of all six intervals. The smallest attainable one-sided p is 2^-11 = 0.00049 (0.00098 doubled), against 0.0001 for the percentile bootstrap.

deff.source_of_larger_values.v: The supplement tables (RV2 dual rows, B = 10 000, ddof 1) cover all 110 contrasts, among them the calls-ratio rows (1.5 to 3.1), the pooled and corrected-reference rows and the Spider-Realistic rows. The sentence of Section 3.2.3 quotes only the four pairs of setup.json, with 2 000 draws, so 1.69 (flash, gated vs single call) is 1.77 with 10 000 draws; the two numbers estimate the same quantity with different Monte Carlo noise.

margin.def.v: Ratio = 1.5 pp / (loop effect), effect = final minus root candidate of the same run ('in') or final minus the separate root-only run ('btw'), 'fixed' = fixed loop, 'gated' = gated loop, pooled = mean of the three backbones. Each interval of the effect is mapped through x -> 1.5 / x (monotone while the effect is positive); when the effect interval reaches 0 the upper end is unbounded and the text says so. Intervals: cl = database-clustered percentile bootstrap, item = item bootstrap, t = cluster-robust t(G-1), sf = exact sign-flip inversion, wide = hull of these four. A wide interval that contains 1 means the data do not say whether the margin is larger or smaller than the effect it protects. margin.sens.*: P1' EX difference (gated minus fixed, pooled) against a margin of half the pooled fixed-loop effect ('half_eff') and against 0.5 pp ('abs05'): lo_* = lower end of the interval of that type, met_* = lo > -margin.

cost.nodisc.def.v: disc = CNY per question with the cache discount as in RV2 (tokens that the API reported as cached are priced at 0.2 of the input price, the 0.2 is an assumption of exp/prices.yaml); nodisc = every prompt token at the full input price. ratio.<b>.<cfg>.vs_<ref>.<mode> = cost of (backbone b, configuration cfg) divided by the cost of the reference, same questions, ratio of sums with the database-clustered interval (.ci) and the item interval (.item_ci); refs: plus_zs = qwen3.7-plus single call, plus_gated = qwen3.7-plus gated loop, self_zs = the same backbone's single call. Per-item costs are rebuilt from the token fields of preds.jsonl (as the RV2 Pareto claims); route.* use the totals of the usage logs (as RV2.cost.*). front.* = Pareto front on point estimates (cost per question against EX). route.per_correct = CNY per correct answer: for route_ca60 the run's cost per question divided by the correct answers per question asked at 60 % coverage; for the other arms cost divided by EX.

cost.nodisc.cached.note.v: Cached prompt tokens are recorded by the API for qwen3.7-plus in every arm (share of prompt tokens per arm in cost.nodisc.cached.plus.<cfg>.share), for qwen3.7-flash in the single-call arm and weakly in the fixed loop and the other pipeline arms, and for qwen3.5-27b in no arm. The discount therefore applies unequally across arms, and depends on run order and prefix reuse rather than on the method; the no-discount figures price every arm alike.

gate.def.v: A question is counted as fired when the loop produced at least one revision (a second candidate in cands.jsonl). Gated loop: the root fails to execute (error or timeout); fixed loop: the Critic score of the current candidate is below 8.5 or the root fails. share = fired / n, with the database-clustered interval (.ci) and the exact Clopper-Pearson interval (.item_ci). n = BIRD dev 1 534 questions (11 databases) and Spider-Realistic 508 questions (19 databases).

gate.hh.def.v: helped (b) = the loop turned a wrong answer right, hurt (c) = right to wrong, paired on the same questions; net = (b - c) / n in percentage points. BIRD dev: 'in' = final minus the root candidate of the same run, 'btw' = final minus the separate root-only run (the keys of RV2.loop.*, repeated here). Spider-Realistic: final minus the root-only run, test-suite EX (the root candidate of a run has no test-suite score). p_two = exact two-sided sign test (binomial, p = 1/2, on the b + c discordant questions; identical to the exact McNemar test), p_one = exact one-sided p that helped exceeds hurt. A sign test treats the discordant questions as independent; it ignores the database clusters.
